title: Phishing email and stolen password
description: Several staff received an email claiming their password would expire. At least one employee entered credentials on a fake login page, and the account was then used from an unfamiliar address. The investigation aims to establish how many users were reached, which account was compromised, and what the attacker did with it.

sources.label: Mail server archive
sources.description: Message store and gateway logs for the company mail system.

sources.label: Employee laptop L-310
sources.description: Laptop of the employee who reported clicking the link.

evidence.title: Original phishing email with full headers
evidence.description: The raw message as delivered to the first reporting employee, including all headers and the body with the link.
evidence.text:
From: "IT Support" <support@corp-helpdesk.example>
Reply-To: helpdesk-verify@mailbox-example.test
Subject: Password expires today - action required
Received: from mx7.mailbox-example.test [203.0.113.45] by mail.corp.example
Body: Your password expires in 2 hours. Verify here to keep access: http://corp-helpdesk.example/login-verify

findings: Sender address imitates the company help desk
The display name says IT Support and the domain looks like the company help desk, but the domain is not owned by the company and the reply address points to a different outside domain.
high
Urgency and a login link
The message creates time pressure and asks the reader to log in through a link to an outside domain, which are typical features of credential phishing.
medium

evidence.title: Warning email from a colleague about the message
evidence.description: A message from a colleague who recognised the email as suspicious and warned others, 40 minutes after delivery.
evidence.text:
From: a.nolan@corp.example
Subject: Re: Password expires today - action required
This does not look right, our help desk never asks us to verify through a link. I did not click it.

evidence.title: Mail gateway delivery log for the phishing message
evidence.description: Gateway log lines showing who the message was delivered to and when.
evidence.text:
2026-09-04 07:31:02 deliver msgid=<7f31@mx7.mailbox-example.test> rcpt=a.nolan@corp.example result=delivered
2026-09-04 07:31:02 deliver msgid=<7f31@mx7.mailbox-example.test> rcpt=r.singh@corp.example result=delivered
Summary: 37 recipients, 37 delivered, 0 quarantined.

findings: Message reached 37 mailboxes without being blocked
All 37 recipients received the message and the gateway did not quarantine any copy.
high
All deliveries in a two-minute window
The mass delivery occurred within two minutes, which is consistent with a single bulk send.
info

evidence.title: Browser history on L-310 showing the fake login page
evidence.description: Web history from the browser on the laptop of the employee who reported clicking the link.
evidence.text:
2026-09-04 08:02:11 visit http://corp-helpdesk.example/login-verify title=Sign in to verify your account
2026-09-04 08:02:49 visit http://corp-helpdesk.example/login-verify/done title=Thank you

findings: Employee visited the fake login page and submitted a form
The history shows a visit to the page followed 38 seconds later by a thank-you page, which fits the entry and submission of credentials.
high

evidence.title: Web proxy log of the form submission
evidence.description: Proxy records for the employee's address during the visit to the fake page.

findings: Form data sent to the outside domain
The proxy recorded a POST of 412 bytes to the fake page, consistent with a username and password being sent.
high

evidence.title: Authentication log showing a login from an unfamiliar address
evidence.description: Sign-in events for the compromised account on the day of the incident.
evidence.text:
2026-09-04 08:41:19 signin user=r.singh result=success ip=203.0.113.52 country=unknown app=webmail mfa=not_required
2026-09-04 08:41:20 signin user=r.singh result=success ip=198.51.100.9 country=home app=mobile mfa=satisfied

findings: Account used from an address the user never uses
About 40 minutes after the credentials were submitted, the account signed in to webmail from an address not seen before, without a second authentication step.
high
Second factor not required for webmail
Webmail sign-in did not ask for the second factor that the mobile sign-in used, which allowed the stolen password to be enough.
medium

evidence.title: Mailbox audit log showing a hidden inbox rule
evidence.description: Audit records of rule changes in the compromised mailbox.
evidence.text: 2026-09-04 08:44:07 rule_created user=r.singh by=203.0.113.52 name=. conditions=subject_contains(password|security|verify) action=move_to(RSS Subscriptions) mark_read=true

findings: Rule hides security-related messages
A rule with a nearly empty name moves any message mentioning passwords, security or verification into an unused folder and marks it as read. This would hide warnings from the real owner.
high

evidence.title: Screenshot of the fake login page
evidence.description: Screenshot of the fake page taken in an isolated test browser.
evidence.notes: Page was taken down two days later.

findings: Fake page copies company logo and layout
The page reproduces the company logo and the colours of the real login page. Small spelling differences in the footer text are visible.
medium

evidence.title: Capture of DNS and web traffic to the phishing domain
evidence.description: Traffic capture at the office perimeter for the domain used by the fake page, from the employee's address.

findings: Page was served over unencrypted web traffic
The fake page was reached over plain HTTP, so the submitted form data crossed the network unencrypted as well.
low

evidence.title: Help desk ticket from the employee who clicked the link
evidence.description: Ticket opened by the employee after being told about the phishing email.
evidence.text: Employee reports clicking the link in the password email at around 08:00 and typing the password on the page. Password has since been reset by the help desk.

evidence.title: Disk image of laptop L-310 browser profile volume
evidence.description: Forensic image of the laptop's user profile volume, taken to look for saved credentials and downloaded files.
evidence.text: NTFS volume 476 GB. Browser profile found at Users/r.singh/AppData/Local. No downloaded executables in the last 14 days.

analyses.notes: Review of saved credentials and downloads in progress.
findings: No malicious downloads found so far
The review has not found downloaded programs on the laptop, which suggests the compromise was limited to the stolen password. The review is not finished.
info

evidence.title: Screenshot taken from the wrong user session
evidence.description: A screenshot of an inbox that was later found to belong to a different employee than the compromised account.
evidence.notes: Taken while signed in as the wrong test user.

withdrawn.reason: Image shows a different employee's mailbox than the compromised account.

links: The delivery log lists the same message that is held as the original email.
The employee's address appears among the 37 recipients and the fake page visit follows delivery.
The proxy records a form submission at the time the history shows the thank-you page.
The sign-in from the unfamiliar address occurs about 40 minutes after the form submission.
The hidden rule was created three minutes after the first sign-in from the unfamiliar address.
